package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
)

// A structured panic argument recovers with its own dynamic type.

type terr struct{}
type T struct{ A int }
type List []int

func try(name string, f func()) {
	defer func() {
		r := recover()
		_, isTerr := r.(terr)
		t, isT := r.(T)
		p, isP := r.(*T)
		l, isL := r.(List)
		_, isString := r.(string)
		fmt.Println(name, isTerr, isT, t, isP, p != nil, isL, l, isString, fmt.Sprint(r))
	}()
	f()
}

func main() {
	try("terr", func() { panic(terr{}) })
	try("T", func() { panic(T{A: 4}) })
	try("ptr", func() { panic(&T{A: 5}) })
	try("list", func() { panic(List{1, 2}) })
	try("map", func() { panic(map[string]int{"k": 1}) })
	// Positive controls: scalar and interface arguments.
	try("string", func() { panic("s") })
	try("int", func() { panic(7) })
	try("iface", func() {
		var v any = T{A: 8}
		panic(v)
	})
	try("error", func() { panic(fmt.Errorf("e")) })
	os.Exit(3)
}
